title: evolve continuation release has NO authority gate — any Bash-capable process (incl. in-cycle agents) can drop a live scope's binding, which the defect-ledger gate treats as anti-tamper lineage evidence
summary: Alignment-audit finding (ADR-0089 gap #2): cmd_continuation.go's release subcommand ships with no operator flag, no confirmation, no env gate — unlike sibling sensitive surfaces (reset-sha -operator, EVOLVE_SHIP_AUTO_CONFIRM). The phase guard blocks in-process Agent/Task only, not Bash invocations of the evolve binary; the registry's 'orchestrator-side only' authority invariant (ADR-0085, cycle-1285 anti-tamper) is silently widened. A lane agent dropping its own scope's binding erases lineage the defect-ledger gate depends on.
root_cause: The CLI was added (cycle-1515) after ADR-0089's acceptance; the authority model the audits demanded for retirement actions was applied to VerifiableBy execution debates but not to the new operator surface.
fix: Gate the release subcommand like its siblings: require -operator (or EVOLVE_OPERATOR_CONFIRM=1), refuse when a live cycle lease exists for the scope's lane unless -force, and log the release into the ledger (who/when/why) so lineage erasure is itself evidenced. Red-first: ungated invocation refuses; gated succeeds; ledger entry pinned.
acceptance: Ungated release refuses with guidance; -operator path succeeds and ledger-records.
notes: Filed from the 3-agent alignment audit. The audits that FAILed lanes twice for missing authority models would fail this CLI too — apply the same standard to console-built surfaces.
